title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', i.e. his study of the group of solutions (α,β,μ) or (λ,f) of the loop equations, which is essentially the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT, acting on Ĝ_{0,3} = π̂1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) = F̂_2. On the preceding pages he defines a map (23) from a set S̃_0M_{0,3} of solutions (α,β,f) to SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)' ⊂ SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) × SL(2,Ẑ). The map 'linearises' a solution by reducing α, β, f to their images in a GL(2,Ẑ)-quotient. The underlying map is F_2 ≅ Γ(2)/±1 ↪ PSL2(Z) → PSL2(Ẑ), with ρ and σ the images of the two standard generators. SG*_{ρ,σ} is a group he built ad hoc out of pairs (α̲,β̲) in GL2 × GL2 together with μ ∈ Ẑ^× and a sign ε_2(μ). Its multiplication is designed so that this reduction is compatible with composition.

On this page he checks that the restriction of (23) to the subset where f is trivial (the 'pure' part, identified with triples (α,β,μ)) is a group homomorphism into SG^±_{ρ,σ}.

1. Composition of automorphisms. An automorphism u = u_{α,β} of Ĝ_{0,3} satisfies u(ρ) = int(α)ρ^μ-type and u(σ) = int(β)σ-type relations. Writing u'' = u_{α'',β''} as the composite of u and u', the 'cocycle relations' (§46 II 5°) give
   (25) α'' = u'(α)α', β'' = u'(β)β', μ'' = μμ'.

2. Linearisation. Choose lifts α̲, β̲, α̲', β̲' in GL(2,Ẑ)^{±} (well defined up to sign) of the images of α, β, α', β'. Choose u̲' ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), in fact in a Borel-type subgroup B'_0(Ẑ), such that
   (26) u̲'(ρ) = int(α̲')ρ, u̲'(σ) = ε_2(μ') int(β̲')σ, det u̲' = μ',
   and similarly for u̲. Here u̲'(·) means conjugation.

3. Compatibility. The reduction then intertwines u' with conjugation by u̲':
   (27) the image of u'(x) equals u̲'(x̲) for all x ∈ Ĝ_{0,3}.

4. Conclusion. Applying the reduction to (25) gives
   (28) α̲'' = u̲'(α̲)α̲', β̲'' = u̲'(β̲)β̲', μ'' = μμ', hence ε_2'' = ε_2 ε_2'.

The next page finishes the check. It writes α̲ = u̲ a̲^{-1} with a̲ in the torus-type centraliser T_ρ, and β̲ = u̲ b̲^{-1} with b̲ in N'_σ. It then computes u̲'(α̲)α̲' = (u̲'u̲)(a̲'a̲)^{-1}, which is exactly the product law in G^×_{ρ,σ}.

Purpose: show that the 'linear shadow' of ĜT (its action on the congruence/SL2 quotient of F̂_2) is a homomorphism into an explicit algebraic-group-like object. This is a step toward understanding which part of the loop-equation solutions is detected by the congruence quotient, which ends up being essentially the cyclotomic character μ plus a coboundary.
errors: Possible order-of-composition inconsistency: the page writes u'' = uu', but the next page's verification uses the product u̲'u̲ (i.e. g'g). This is harmless if the convention is read consistently, but the notation as written is ambiguous.
Statement (27) is asserted with '(cf ...)', i.e. with no reference filled in. It depends on the choice of u̲' in (26) existing, which is supposed rather than proved here ('supposons qu'on trouve').
The lifts α̲, β̲ are determined only up to sign. That the sign bookkeeping via ε_2 is consistent is asserted rather than checked on this page.

ideas.what: Cocycle relations for composing automorphisms of F̂_2 given by pairs (α,β,μ): α''=u'(α)α', β''=u'(β)β', μ''=μμ'
ideas.modern_name: Multiplication law of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT (Drinfeld's composition (λ1,f1)(λ2,f2))
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without formulas

ideas.what: Linearisation of ĜT-type automorphisms via F_2 ≅ Γ(2) → SL2/GL2(Ẑ): the induced automorphism of the congruence quotient is conjugation by an element u̲ of GL2(Ẑ) with det = μ
ideas.modern_name: Action of ĜT / Gal(Q̄/Q) on the congruence completion of Γ(2); its factorisation through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Asada and others (1990s); classical for the Galois action on modular curves

ideas.what: Ad hoc group SG*_{ρ,σ} of pairs (α̲,β̲,μ,ε) with α̲ = u̲a̲^{-1}, a̲ in the centraliser of ρ, and β̲ = u̲b̲^{-1}, b̲ in the normaliser of σ, with product (u̲'u̲)(a̲'a̲)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Group of solutions of a 'linearised loop equation'; a transporter/torsor-type construction

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping verification ('pour me rassurer') that an ad hoc composition law makes the linearisation map a homomorphism. The underlying idea of comparing ĜT with its image in the congruence/GL2 quotient is known in the literature. Nothing new beyond the specific notation for his group SG*_{ρ,σ}.
transcription_corrections: The page number written at the bottom left is 384 (the archive sheet number). The next page carries '385' at the bottom while its header reads '499'.
Line 2: the object looks like '$\tilde{S}_0 M_{0,3}$ [o]' (consistent with the S_0M^{!~}_{0,3} of the previous page) rather than '\hat{\mathfrak M}_{0,3}'.
Line 3: the image reads roughly 'aux (α,β,μ) pour lesquels f=1' (the f is barely legible, with a superscript ±1), not 'f^{±1}_{\sim}'.
Line 3, the insertion: it reads 'dans le groupe SG^{±}_{ρ,σ}' (the subscript may be written ρ,σ).
(26): the second component reads 'u̲'(σ) = ε_2(μ') int(β̲')(σ)'.
Last lines: the marginal note reads 'en plus de μ''=μμ' d'où ε''_2 = ε_2 ε'_2'.
